issues.description: Method name mismatch: The exercise requires a public method named singFarmSong() on class Farm (problem statement and template declare and call singFarmSong()), but the solution implementation exposes a method named playFarmSong() instead. Specifically, problem_statement.md and the template's Farm.java define/use singFarmSong(), while solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java only provides public void playFarmSong(), so code that expects Farm.singFarmSong() (including the provided Main) will not find the required method and may fail to compile or behave inconsistently.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's public API match the specification: in solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java either rename the method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method that delegates to playFarmSong(). Ensure the method signature is public void singFarmSong() so the template Main and the problem statement references compile and behave as expected.

issues.description: The exercise asks for a Farm method named singFarmSong() (problem statement and template), but the solution implementation defines playFarmSong(). Specifically: problem_statement.md and the template Farm.java declare/expect singFarmSong(); solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares playFarmSong(); solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java still references singFarmSong() in a commented example. Students reading the problem or using the template will look for singFarmSong() but the reference solution uses a different name, preventing a clear one-to-one mapping and causing confusion about which method to implement or invoke.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java:playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), and update any callers (e.g., Main) accordingly. Alternatively, if playFarmSong() is preferred, change the problem statement and template to refer to playFarmSong() so all three artifacts use the same identifier.
